newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BILARDO LEAVES SEVILLA AFTER JUST FOUR GAMES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BILARDO LEAVES SEVILLA AFTER JUST FOUR GAMES.

text.p: Argentine World Cup-winning coach Carlos Bilardo has resigned as boss of struggling Sevilla less than a month after he took over at the Spanish first division club.

"From the start nothing went well," said Bilardo, who guided Argentina to success in the 1986 World Cup but had lost three of his four games in charge in his second spell in the southern Spanish city.
He had returned to take over from Jose Antonio Camacho, but found himself unable to cope with the underlying instability of a club wracked by boardroom conflict and financial problems.
The tension came to a head in Sunday's 4-1 home defeat by Logrones, during which several policemen incurred minor injuries while trying to restrain fans attacking the chairman's box.
Chairman Jose Maria Gonzalez has been under constant fire from supporters after a series of well-publicised scandals.
Newspapers alleged there were forged signatures in a transfer document and that Sevilla paid Barcelona for midfielder Robert Prosinecki with a blank cheque.
Previous manager Camacho failed to turn the team around and Brazilian striker Bebeto went back home after just seven weeks saying he was worried about getting paid.
On the field things have been even worse.
Sevilla, a side accustomed to fighting for a UEFA Cup place, have slipped to second-from-bottom in a season in which four teams are automatically relegated.
Bilardo will be replaced on a temporary basis by second-team coach Julian Rubio.
